report.say: The deep read landed. Four parallel readers covered all 16 corroborated transcripts plus slides and the Ipeirotis folder, and the write-up is on disk. It caught real overclaims: the NYU "they'll share course materials" line is actually Columbia's Toubia & Ben Sliman; the "don't use AI for market research" framing contradicts LaSala and Griffel; Canetti's company is AGNT, not Skej. Nothing in the corpus supports privacy or train-on-data claims. Talks 15 and 16 have zero artifacts — hard gaps.
produced: gandalf/corpus-read-2026-08-06/SYMPOSIUM-CORPUS-READ.md — theme-by-talk map plus the can't-back list
gandalf/corpus-read-2026-08-06/draft.json — the RAW draft sent to the grading engine
Correction: the "email us for all course materials" offer is Columbia's (Toubia & Ben Sliman), not NYU's
Correction: "don't rely on AI for market research" overclaims — LaSala and Griffel both teach AI-for-research; corpus supports "AI gathers, humans judge"
Correction: Canetti's company is AGNT; "Skej" is a program-listing artifact
Gap: no privacy / train-on-data content anywhere in the corpus — those claims need outside sources
Gap: talks 15 (Sturt) and 16 (Song Ma) have no artifacts at all
MIT→Columbia lineage confirmed (Ramakrishnan's HODL inspired Guetta; Beasley piloted Socrat in Broadie's class)
report.needs: The four themes were never pinned verbatim anywhere, so the read derived them from your brief (build-with-AI · AI-mechanics curriculum · business-problems/startups · AI-as-teaching-infrastructure) and cross-walked every talk to SUMMARY.md's five threads as a hedge. Are those four labels the ones you want the deck built on?
report.recommend: Read the can't-back list first — three deck claims you were likely to make are wrong as stated, and fixing them now is cheaper than after the slides exist.
